summary: Cambodian officials and experts are pushing for a peaceful resolution to ongoing border tensions with Thailand. summary: Incoming Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has confirmed that the cancellation of the 2001 MOU 44 regarding overlapping maritime claims with Cambodia will be a formal government policy. The move follows his campaign promises and recent meetings with defense and naval leaders. The MOU, which has seen no breakthrough in over 20 years, involves significant undersea resources and maritime boundaries that the Thai military insists must be negotiated alongside land markers.

summary: An analysis suggests Thailand is engaging in a sophisticated diplomatic campaign to reshape its global image while maintaining military positions on disputed land. summary: In a move with regional diplomatic implications, Cambodia's parliament has passed its first dedicated cybercrime law. The legislation targets online scam centers which have been a major point of tension between Cambodia and neighboring Thailand. Justice Minister Keut Rith stated the law aims to 'clean up' operations that have harmed international victims and impacted the national economy. Penalties include up to 10 years in prison for organized scams.

summary: Journalists were given a tour of the O'Smach Resort complex, a 197-acre site seized by the Thai military in December 2025 during border clashes. The military claims the site was used as a base for Cambodian attacks and as an 'industrial-scale' scam hub where 10,000 people lived and worked to defraud victims globally, including Americans who lost $21 billion in 2025. Evidence found included foreign SIM cards and scripts in multiple languages.

summary: Assessments of the Preah Vihear Temple site reveal 562 points of damage following military clashes in late 2025. Restoration experts estimate that stabilizing the 11th-century structure to prevent collapse will take 5 to 10 years, while a full restoration could span 30 years. Work is currently hampered by unexploded ordnance (UXO) littering the UNESCO World Heritage site.

summary: A 2026 survey by the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute reveals that while nearly 39% of Southeast Asian respondents believe ASEAN actively mediated the Thailand-Cambodia border conflict, over 34% still view the bloc as slow and ineffective. The conflict, which displaced over one million people in late 2025 before a December ceasefire, highlighted ASEAN's internal constraints and reliance on outside powers like the U.S. and China for mediation.
summaryKh: ការស្ទង់មតិឆ្នាំ 2026 ដោយវិទ្យាស្ថាន ISEAS-Yusof Ishak បានបង្ហាញថា ខណៈដែលអ្នកឆ្លើយសំណួរជិត 39% ក្នុងតំបន់អាស៊ានជឿថា អាស៊ានបានសម្របសម្រួលយ៉ាងសកម្មក្នុងជម្លោះព្រំដែនថៃ-កម្ពុជា ប៉ុន្តែជាង 34% នៅតែមើលឃើញថា ប្លុកនេះមានភាពយឺតយ៉ាវ និងគ្មានប្រសិទ្ធភាព។ ជម្លោះនេះបានធ្វើឱ្យមនុស្សជាងមួយលាននាក់ភៀសខ្លួននៅចុងឆ្នាំ 2025 មុនពេលមានបទឈប់បាញ់ក្នុងខែធ្នូ ដែលបង្ហាញពីកម្រិតកំណត់ផ្ទៃក្នុងរបស់អាស៊ាន និងការពឹងផ្អែកលើមហាអំណាចខាងក្រៅដូចជាសហរដ្ឋអាមេរិក និងចិនសម្រាប់ការសម្របសម្រួល។
summaryTh: ผลสำรวจปี 2026 โดยสถาบัน ISEAS-Yusof Ishak พบว่าแม้เกือบ 39% ของผู้ตอบแบบสอบถามในอาเซียนจะเชื่อว่าอาเซียนมีบทบาทเชิงรุกในการไกล่เกลี่ยความขัดแย้งชายแดนไทย-กัมพูชา แต่กว่า 34% ยังมองว่าอาเซียนทำงานล่าช้าและขาดประสิทธิภาพ ความขัดแย้งนี้ทำให้คนกว่าหนึ่งล้านคนต้องอพยพในช่วงปลายปี 2025 ก่อนจะมีการหยุดยิงในเดือนธันวาคม ซึ่งสะท้อนถึงข้อจำกัดภายในของอาเซียนและการต้องพึ่งพาชาติมหาอำนาจภายนอกอย่างสหรัฐฯ และจีนในการไกล่เกลี่ย

summary: The State of South-east Asia 2026 report reveals that while 38.9% of regional respondents believe ASEAN took active steps to mediate the 2025 border conflict, nearly 35% still view the bloc as 'slow and ineffective.' summary: The annual Thai military conscription lottery has seen a nearly 50% increase in volunteers this year following deadly border clashes with Cambodia in late 2025. Officials noted that tens of thousands of citizens remain displaced from the border regions where tensions still persist.

summary: The Royal Thai Army is accelerating the construction of 182 civilian shelters along the border with Cambodia to protect residents following recent escalations. Although active clashes have eased, Army chief Gen Phana Klaewplodthuk emphasized that security remains a top priority. Currently, 117 shelters have been completed, with the overall project being over 80% finished. The shelters are distributed between the Burapha and Suranaree Task Forces.

summary: The Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFAIC) issued a formal protest against Thai armed forces for alleged 'unlawful activities' in border areas of Battambang and Oddar Meanchey. Cambodia claims these actions violate sovereignty and de-escalation measures agreed upon in December 2025, and maintains it does not recognize any boundary lines unilaterally claimed by Thailand.

summary: Phnom Penh has called for a swift return to the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) talks to prevent further border instability. Cambodia continues to accuse Thai troops of occupying land in violation of the December ceasefire, while Thailand maintains it will follow its own schedule for resuming diplomacy.

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet announced that Cambodia will prioritize direct bilateral talks with Thailand over international legal action at the ICJ to resolve border disputes. He cited the need for speed and efficiency to help residents living in uncertain border areas. This follows a policy shift by new Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul, who also signaled a preference for peaceful negotiation. Both nations currently maintain troop positions under the 'KL Accord' to prevent accidental clashes while technical teams survey the land.

summary: The Royal Thai Navy stated on April 14, 2026, that it has not received any formal request from Cambodia to reopen border checkpoints in Chanthaburi and Trat provinces. The navy emphasized that national security remains the priority and the situation on the ground remains quiet following the December 2025 ceasefire.

summary: A UN report released on April 17 warns of a "double shock" following the 2025 Thailand-Cambodia border conflict. summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a formal protest on April 19 regarding Thai military activities observed on April 18. The protest alleges that Thai forces are consolidating an 'illegal occupation' by constructing observation posts, bunkers, and expanding roads in disputed areas across Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey, and Pursat provinces. Cambodia claims these actions violate the UN Charter and ASEAN agreements, urging Thailand to halt unilateral actions to prevent further escalation.

summaryKh: នៅក្នុងវេទិកា UN ECOSOC នៅទីក្រុងញូវយ៉ក តំណាងអចិន្ត្រៃយ៍របស់ប្រទេសថៃ លោក Cherdchai Chaivaivid បានចោទប្រកាន់ថា ការវាយប្រហាររបស់កម្ពុជានៅខែកក្កដា និងធ្នូ ឆ្នាំ 2025 បានសម្លាប់ជនស៊ីវិលថៃ 19 នាក់ និងធ្វើឱ្យមនុស្ស 400,000 នាក់ភៀសខ្លួន។ ប្រទេសថៃបានប្រើប្រាស់សិទ្ធិការពារខ្លួនក្រោមមាត្រា 51 នៃធម្មនុញ្ញអង្គការសហប្រជាជាតិ និងបានលើកឡើងពីកង្វល់ជុំវិញគ្រាប់មីនថ្មីដែលត្រូវបានគេចោទថាត្រូវបានដាក់នៅតាមតំបន់ព្រំដែន ទោះបីជាមានកិច្ចខិតខំប្រឹងប្រែងបោសសម្អាតមីនអន្តរជាតិក៏ដោយ។
summaryTh: ในการประชุม UN ECOSOC ที่นิวยอร์ก นายเชิดชาย ใช้ไววิทย์ เอกอัครราชทูตผู้แทนถาวรไทยประจำ UN กล่าวหาว่าการโจมตีของกัมพูชาเมื่อเดือนกรกฎาคมและธันวาคม 2568 ทำให้พลเรือนไทยเสียชีวิต 19 ราย และต้องอพยพกว่า 4 แสนคน โดยไทยได้ใช้สิทธิ์ป้องกันตนเองตามกฎบัตร UN มาตรา 51 พร้อมแสดงความกังวลเรื่องการวางทุ่นระเบิดใหม่ในพื้นที่ชายแดน

summary: Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced that the National Security Council has confirmed the abolition of the 2001 maritime Memorandum of Understanding (MOU 44) with Cambodia. Officials cited a lack of progress over several decades and noted that future negotiations will occur under the framework of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

summary: Thailand's Defence Minister stated that border crossings with Cambodia will remain closed until specific security and sovereignty terms are met. The decision follows recent tensions and is intended to protect national security. The military continues to monitor the situation through the Thai-Cambodian Regional Border Committee to ensure compliance with joint statements.

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Bangkok on Friday. Wang Yi expressed hopes for improved relations between Thailand and Cambodia following two rounds of armed conflict in 2025. The Thai government stated that both nations also prioritize tackling cross-border cyber scams.

summary: Cambodian officials at the UN ECOSOC Forum rejected Thai allegations that Cambodia is a global hub for cybercrime, labeling it a 'scam narrative' used to justify border aggression. Cambodia claimed that 2025 border clashes, which resulted in over 100 deaths, were caused by Thai incursions into its sovereign territory.
summaryKh: មន្ត្រីកម្ពុជានៅវេទិកា UN ECOSOC បានច្រានចោលការចោទប្រកាន់របស់ថៃដែលថា កម្ពុជាគឺជាមជ្ឈមណ្ឌលសកលសម្រាប់ឧក្រិដ្ឋកម្មតាមអ៊ីនធឺណិត។ កម្ពុជាបានចោទប្រកាន់ថៃថាបានប្រើ 'រឿងនិទានបោកប្រាស់' ដើម្បីបង្វែរអារម្មណ៍ពីការចូលលុកលុយដែនដី។ នេះកើតឡើងបន្ទាប់ពីការអះអាងរបស់ថៃថា ជម្លោះព្រំដែនក្នុងឆ្នាំ 2025 បានបណ្តាលឱ្យជនស៊ីវិល 19 នាក់ស្លាប់ និងមានការភៀសខ្លួនយ៉ាងច្រើននៅខាងភាគីថៃ។

summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in Bangkok to encourage peaceful dialogue following two rounds of armed border clashes between Thailand and Cambodia. summary: Thailand's National Security Council (NSC) has approved a proposal to unilaterally cancel the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) regarding maritime boundary disputes in the Gulf of Thailand. summary: Cambodia is increasingly relying on the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) to protect its maritime rights as Thailand considers revoking the 2001 Memorandum of Understanding (MoU44). Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul reportedly confirmed preparations to cancel the pact due to a lack of progress in negotiations over overlapping claims in the Gulf of Thailand. Cambodia, which officially joined UNCLOS in March 2026, views the convention as a strategic 'insurance policy' that puts both nations on equal legal footing under international law.
